purpose: Second round of three distinct Qibla screen design proposals; select before implementation

concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE complete polished mobile UI screenshot for the Qibla page of Halovat, an Uzbek prayer app. This is a NEW design proposal, not code, not an illustration poster. Portrait 9:19.5 aspect ratio, one screen only, no hardware frame, no presentation margins, no collage, no watermark. Beautifully readable iOS system typography, deliberate layout and realistic tappable controls. Purpose: help user turn phone toward Qibla. Data: target Qibla bearing 240°, phone heading 188°, turn right by 52°. Use clear Uzbek copy. Include "Qibla", a small "Toshkent" location indicator and "GPS · ±17 m", central guidance "O‘ngga 52° buring", compact technical readings "Qibla 240°" and "Telefon 188°", minimal outlined "Qayta sozlash" action and a "Yaqin masjidlar" navigation action near bottom. No profile icon in header, no maps, no mosque list, no extra features, no stats cards or prayer time cards.
Include status bar, bottom safe area and persistent native five-tab navbar: home outline icon "Bosh sahifa", calendar outline icon "Namozlar", circular dotted tasbeeh icon "Tasbeh", compass icon "Qibla" selected, person outline icon "Profil". Tabbar not obscured. All fits on a single screen.
Halovat brand: warm ivory #FAF9F5, dark emerald #064E3B, mint #BFF1DB/#77D3AF. Restrained premium, purposeful space, minimal bordered controls, no bubbly glass buttons or ornamental patterns. Must look bespoke and buildable in React Native.
A modest sculptural 3D Kaaba asset connects to the app: recognizably black cuboid, no roof, gold embroidered band near top, correct golden door on one side, high-quality material and lighting. Do not turn it into a mosque. Angle geometry should express turn right. Avoid prior layouts: NO standard full circular compass, NO semicircular speedometer, NO green rectangular hero containing huge Kaaba on an elliptical compass pedestal. This round must have a genuinely new composition.
DIRECTION 4: "Bearing strip / premium navigation instrument". Warm ivory screen with a small centered native header. Top-third contains one elegant moderate-size photoreal 3D Kaaba with very soft shadow, floating in open ivory space, no card around it. Beneath the Kaaba a compact eyebrow "QIBLA YO‘NALISHI" then huge editorial "240°", showing target bearing. Core interaction is a full-width HORIZONTAL bearing ruler, finely etched like a high-end measuring instrument, on a subtle pale-gray horizontal band. Thin ticks and legible numbers 180°, 200°, 220°, 240°, 260°. A fixed slim black current-heading cursor near 188°, small text "Telefon" under cursor; the 240° tick is mint-accented and has a tiny Kaaba target symbol. A thin emerald right-pointing arrow/bracket between current cursor and target explains that the phone must turn right. Below the ruler, large clean "52°" at left and "O‘ngga buring" with a small right-turn icon at right, separated by purposeful white space. Then small location row with GPS and discreet location-edit icon. Bottom actions use a compact native outlined recalibration button and an understated mosque navigation row with a line icon and chevron. No huge circular dial. Scandinavian precision meets calm Islamic app. Clear, simple and tasteful, with nuanced tiny geometry.

DIRECTION 5: "The path / spatial guidance". Build a gorgeous LIGHT ivory screen with a flowing spatial directional composition, not a dial. Compact title aligned left; location and GPS in a discreet row under title. Main scene occupies the middle 45% of screen: a subtle pale-mint plane receding in perspective into the distance; at its upper-right destination a beautifully lit modest 3D Kaaba sits naturally on the plane. Near the foreground center, a small simple phone-position marker; a single slender dark-emerald curved directional ribbon/line leads from foreground marker to the Kaaba at upper right. The ribbon curves gently RIGHT and has one precise arrowhead. Sparse perspective guide lines, just two or three, help orientation; no grid, no map, no buildings or landscape. Soft shadows and a warm studio look, as if a calm minimalist navigation sculpture is embedded directly in the screen. At the visual base of scene a large "52°" and "O‘ngga buring" in balanced two-line editorial typography. A small grounded caption "Qibla 240° · Telefon 188°". Only one very quiet hairline separates the instrument from the controls. Recalibration is a discreet outlined rounded rectangle with circular-arrow icon, NOT a giant full-width pill. "Yaqin masjidlar" is an understated wide pale-mint navigation row at bottom, with a tiny mosque outline and slim right chevron. Native bottom tabbar stays visible. Calm, compelling, familiar to use but distinctly non-template. This is illustrative sensor guidance, NOT a live AR camera UI.

DIRECTION 6: "Night instrument / typography first". A distinct FULL DARK MODE design, ink-green background #0E1914 throughout, subtle #192820 surfaces, warm off-white typography, restrained mint highlights, tiny pale-gold accent only on Kaaba. No large rectangular green hero and no traditional compass dial. Header top left "Qibla", tiny "Toshkent" / "GPS · ±17 m" on top right in a quiet compact block. Main display is a tall thin-outline octagonal directional instrument, an elegant technical frame open and airy with only 8 small direction marks, absolutely NOT a full circle or half circle. A small beautifully crafted 3D Kaaba sits at the fixed top target, mostly black material with gold band and door made clearly visible against dark surface through restrained rim light. Within the instrument a slender mint needle with a tiny central hub points upper-right 52 degrees from vertical; a faint dashed line to the top target clarifies the right-turn gap. Sparse UI, no colored luminous effects or neon sci-fi decoration. Oversized monospaced off-white "52°" is the visual focal point under the needle, asymmetrically offset slightly left, with a compact right-turn arrow and "O‘ngga buring" to its right. Below, a single thin line and two small typography columns "Qibla 240°", "Telefon 188°". Controls at bottom: a quiet minimal stroke "Qayta sozlash" button and a dark mint-tinted nearby-mosques row with fine outlined mosque icon and chevron. Dark native bottom tab bar, Qibla active mint; all five icons and labels present and readable. Feels like a premium quiet instrument, finely designed typography, human-friendly and easy to scan.
